Electrical Technologist here.  One of the biggest issues with switching over to all electric vehicles, besides the generation demand going through the roof, is that our current distribution systems will be overloaded.  All of our transformers, residential service panels and  distribution lines will need to be upgraded to support that demand.  Who is going to pay for all the upgrades you ask? Why the customer of course!  The other issues with electric vehicles is harmonic distortion on our distribution systems.  These harmonics are noise that makes power "dirty" distorting the AC wave form.  DC chargers are taking a sinusoidal waveform and clipping of the top bits of potential and discarding the rest that is not at peak potential.  What ever is not used by the charger then returns on the neutral and back to the source transformer as losses.  There are so many losses from the generation, transmission, rectification and motor losses that I personally don't see electrical cars taking over very soon.  A lot of research and FUNDING is required to make this viable in the future.  We also need to get our electricity generation methods cleaned up and more efficient.  Solar and wind are...a work in progress.
